criteria.criterion: The audit command validates manifest structure and reports malformed records without a traceback.
criteria.test: tasks/skills-59f828ed3d49/tests/hidden/cases.py: main() checks only malformed top-level JSON (`malformed.json`) and malformed policy; no malformed record-shape/type cases are exercised.
criteria.gap: Missing coverage for non-object records, extra/missing record keys, invalid path/bytes/sha256 types, duplicate JSON keys, empty manifests, and report shape/diagnostic guarantees. The implementation does not reject invalid bytes/hash records before filesystem auditing, so malformed records can receive incidental BYTE_MISMATCH/HASH_MISMATCH errors.

criteria.criterion: Unsafe, non-canonical, missing, non-regular, and symlink-escaping paths are rejected.
criteria.test: tasks/skills-59f828ed3d49/tests/hidden/cases.py: main() checks one `../secret` traversal, one duplicate path, and one escaping symlink (conditionally skipped if symlinks are unavailable).
criteria.gap: No tests cover absolute paths, NULs, backslashes, dot components, repeated separators, trailing separators, missing files, directories, special files, dangling/internal symlinks, or duplicate policy paths. The conditional symlink test can silently provide no coverage on platforms without symlink support. Output safety is path-based and can be bypassed with a hard link to an audited input; the implementation also has a TOCTOU gap between resolution and reading.

criteria.criterion: Existing file bytes, byte counts, SHA-256 values, and policy constraints are checked accurately.
criteria.test: tasks/skills-59f828ed3d49/tests/hidden/cases.py: main() checks one correct manifest, one wrong byte count/hash, extension and max-size violations, and one forbidden path.
criteria.gap: No boundary tests for zero-byte files, exact max size, extension edge cases, unreadable/special files, policy allowed-extension validation, malformed policy lists, duplicate policy paths, required-path success/failure, or hash/byte validation with malformed record types. There is no oracle comparing independently generated JSON/text error details beyond selected codes.

criteria.criterion: JSON and text reports are deterministic, sorted, and sent to the requested output channel with correct exit status.
criteria.test: tasks/skills-59f828ed3d49/tests/hidden/cases.py: main() compares two successful JSON runs with reversed records, checks one successful text file-output run, and checks selected failure return codes.
criteria.gap: No failed text-report test, no stdout text-mode test, no exact JSON serialization/key/order check, no deterministic comparison of equivalent failing manifests, no output-write failure test, no stderr diagnostic assertions for operational errors, and no explicit check that reports are emitted exactly once. Paths/details containing newlines can violate the promised one-error-per-line text format.

findings: The verifier is materially exploitable: `tests/test.sh` runs a readable `/tests/hidden/cases.py`, converts any assertion failure into reward 0 while always exiting 0, and exposes the test location and `MANIFEST_AUDIT_APP` to the candidate process. A submission can detect or special-case the bundled tests instead of implementing the specification. Add an isolated oracle/verifier boundary, avoid exposing test sources, and make verifier failures fail closed.

The acceptance tests are a single monolithic `main()` with no independent failure reporting or timeout. A hang, resource exhaustion, or unexpected verifier exception is not robustly handled, and the log is not surfaced as a structured grading result.

The provided solution has an actionable safety defect not caught by tests: output protection compares resolved pathnames, so an output path that is a hard link to an audited input can overwrite the audited inode. Use file-identity checks (for example, compare `stat()` device/inode before writing) and test hard-link aliases.

The provided solution does not preserve the required one-line-per-error text representation for valid paths containing newline characters; canonical-path validation permits newlines, while text emission interpolates them directly. Either reject control characters as part of the path contract or escape them and test the behavior.

The manifest parser accepts JSON objects with duplicate keys because `json.load()` silently keeps the last value. If exact schema validation includes the serialized input, use an `object_pairs_hook` to reject duplicates and add a test.

The source receipt records URLs, commit identifiers, inspected paths, and a license hash, but does not include the inspected source, hashes of the relevant files, command timestamps, or evidence for the claim that no benchmark/evaluation task was reused. Provenance and originality remain assertions rather than independently verifiable evidence.

The baseline receipt only shows a few command transcripts and a missing deliverable check. It does not establish that the baseline verifier was run end-to-end, that the image exactly matches the declared environment, or that no preexisting `/app/manifest_audit.py` behavior contaminated evaluation. Treat baseline/oracle clearance as unproven and add reproducible image and verifier checks.

Difficulty is overstated relative to the actual grading: the task is mostly straightforward JSON/path/hash plumbing, has no resource-pressure cases, no race or platform matrix, and only one shallow visible hidden-case script. Add adversarial filesystem types, malformed JSON/schema cases, output-channel failures, hard links/races where feasible, and stronger independent oracles before labeling it medium security difficulty.
